newsitem.title: UK: Dutch stocks have more to gain in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch stocks have more to gain in 1997.

text.p: Amsterdam stocks have further to go in 1997 but their gains will not be as striking as this year, a Reuters survey of the outlook for world stock markets found on Wednesday.
The average of 10 forecasts for the AEX index anticipated a move to around 640 points from current levels of around 610-620, but the range spread from 578 to 687.

By 1998, for which four forecasts were given, the market was seen moving up further, although some analysts warned of a correction from historically high levels. The AEX touched an all-time high of 636.75 on December 3.
The following is a selection of quotes from analysts who gave AEX forecasts to the survey:
MICHEL VAN DER STEE, STRATEGIST AT F VAN LANSCHOT BANKIERS

"In our basic scenario, we still have further to gain. Our 1997 forecast of 650 is a bit conservative but...we are not at the peak of the earnings cycle yet. If interest rates don't move up quickly, we think 1998 could be another good year for stocks."
CORNE ZANDBERGEN, HEAD OF INSTITUTIONAL RESEARCH AT GENERALE BANK

"We are positive on 1997 but we see a number of small problems. Share prices have moved up very quickly in recent months. We expect interest rates will show an upward movement in 1997 and that could have a negative impact on share price developments in the Netherlands and world wide. The Dutch share market (used to have) a discount to its European competitors. Now it's zero and may even be a small premium."

"We see the market coming off in the first half of 1997 and then recovering through the year. Looking back to the last 25 years it is clear that the indices are far above the long-term trendline and will have to go back to it eventually."
